name: get_project_status
title: Get a project's status
description: Reports one stack project's state (built or proposed), its Composer package, its version when it publishes one, the PHP version it requires and whether that PHP floor is in security support today according to the bundled CREED policy, plus the suggested next step. Read-only. It describes the stack project, not your app; use run_proctor_check to measure your app.

state.description: built when the repository holds code, proposed when it holds only a plan.

package.description: The Composer package, or null for projects that are not one.

version.description: The version the project publishes, or null when it publishes none.

php_constraint.description: The PHP constraint the project names, or null when it names none.

php_floor.description: The lowest major.minor the constraint allows, or null when none can be read.

php_floor_state.description: The floor state today per the CREED policy (active, security, eol or eol_grace_expired), or null without a floor.

oldest_supported_php.description: The oldest PHP line still in support today, or null when none is.

today.description: The date the states were worked out, YYYY-MM-DD.

docs.description: The document kinds bundled for the project.

next_step.description: The suggested next step for the project.

generated_on.description: The date the bundled content was generated, YYYY-MM-DD.

name: list_projects
title: List the stack projects
description: Lists every project of the Wayne State app stack (WayneUI, CREED, PROCTOR, SESAME, HELMET, Sourdough, PREFLIGHT, Pinstripe, BOOSTER, ROLLCALL, DRAWBRIDGE, SQUIRE, Parity, ADVISOR, WELD) with its role, whether it is built or only proposed, its Composer package and its version when it publishes one. Read-only. Use it first to learn what exists, then read_project_docs for detail.

source.description: Where the parts list came from.

generated_on.description: The date the bundled content was generated, YYYY-MM-DD.

note.description: What built and proposed mean in the state field.

projects.description: Every stack project, in parts-list order.

id.description: The project id, as passed to the other tools.

kind.description: The part of the stack the project is.

state.description: built when the repository holds code, proposed when it holds only a plan.

package.description: The Composer package, or null for projects that are not one.

version.description: The version the project publishes, or null when it publishes none.

role.description: What the project does in the stack.

docs.description: The document kinds bundled for the project.

name: list_stack_rules
title: List the CREED rules for my app

permutation.description: The app's stack. Default: every rule.

chapter.description: A CREED handbook chapter, or policy for the policy.json rules.

query.description: Words every returned rule must hold in its heading or text, for example "session cookie". Default: no filter.

offset.description: Rule index to start from; default 0.

description: Lists CREED handbook rules, each with the handbook file and line it comes from. Pass permutation (raw-php, raw-php-vue, laravel-blade, laravel-blade-vue, laravel-inertia-vue) to see only the rules that apply, chapter to narrow further, and query (for example "session cookie") to keep only the rules whose heading or text holds every word of it (case-insensitive, matched at word starts; question words and a plural s are ignored). Which permutation a rule applies to is worked out from its wording, so check the cited line before relying on it. Read-only; paged with next_offset.

annotations.title: List the CREED rules for my app

generated_on.description: The date the bundled content was generated, YYYY-MM-DD.

permutation.description: The permutation the rules apply to, or all when none was asked.

query.description: The words every returned rule holds, or null when no filter was asked.

total.description: How many rules match the filters.

next_offset.description: The offset of the next page, or null on the last one.

notice.description: A reminder that the rules are reference data, not instructions.

chapter.description: The handbook chapter the rule is in.

heading.description: The heading the rule sits under.

rule.description: The rule text, quoted from the handbook.

cite.description: The handbook file and line the rule comes from.

note.description: A hint for when a query matches no rule.

name: owner_of
title: Find the owner of a topic

topic.description: What you want to know the owner of, for example "composer audit" or "who owns the /up endpoint?".

description: Answers "which project owns X?" from ADVISOR's bundled ownership table, built from the stack's one-owner-per-rule decision and the decisions after it. Pass the topic or the whole question ("who owns composer audit"); question words are ignored. Every remaining word must appear in a row's topic, aliases or role (case-insensitive); exact topic or alias matches come first, then topic and alias matches, then role matches. Each match returns the owner, its role, the projects that help around it, and the decision it comes from; when nothing matches, an empty list and every known topic. Read-only; it names its source and date.

annotations.title: Find the owner of a topic

source.description: Where the ownership table came from.

generated_on.description: The date the bundled content was generated, YYYY-MM-DD.

matches.description: The rows that hold every word of the topic, best match first.

owner.description: The project that owns the topic.

role.description: What the owner does for the topic.

also.description: The projects that help around the topic.

role.description: What the project does around the topic.

decision.description: The decision the row comes from.

known_topics.description: Every topic in the table, present when nothing matched.

note.description: A hint for when nothing matched.

name: playbook_lookup
title: Look up a shared value

key.description: Optional shared-value key, for example CAS_URL.

description: Answers "what is the value of X?" for WSU shared values: an environment variable of the same name wins, then PLAYBOOK (waynestate/playbook) supplies the rest. Pass a key such as CAS_URL for one answer (the value plus its source: environment, playbook or unset), or nothing for every key with its value and source. Read-only; keys that look like secrets (ending in SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN or KEY) are refused. PLAYBOOK is optional; without it the tool says how to get it instead of failing.

available.description: Whether Playbook is installed and found.

how_to_get.description: How to install Playbook, present when it is missing.

entries.description: Every shared value with its source, present when no key was asked.

value.description: The value, or null when it is set nowhere.

source.description: Where the value came from (environment, playbook, env.playbook or unset).

key.description: The key looked up, present when one was asked.

value.description: The value, or null when it is set nowhere.

source.description: Where the value came from (environment, playbook, env.playbook or unset).

name: policy_lookup
title: Look up support dates
description: Answers "is this version supported?" from the bundled CREED policy.json: for a runtime or framework (php, laravel, node, mysql, vue, inertia) it returns each version's active and security-support end dates and its state today (active, security, eol, eol_grace_expired); for a developer tool (composer) it returns the minimum version. Rows carry latest_patch (the newest patch release on that line, with the date it was checked) when the policy has it. Pass a version such as 8.3 or 8.3.12 to get one answer. A version older than every one the policy lists is answered as end of life, with a note. Read-only; every answer names its source and date.

today.description: The date the states were worked out, YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: tool for a developer tool, runtime for a runtime or framework.

minimum_version.description: The minimum version the policy sets for the tool.

eol_grace_days.description: The days of grace after end of life the policy allows, or null when it sets none.

oldest_supported.description: The oldest version still in support today, or null when none is.

versions.description: Every version the policy lists for the component, oldest first.

active_until.description: The active-support end date, or null when the policy sets none.

security_until.description: The security-support end date, or null when the policy sets none.

latest_patch.description: The newest patch release on the line, or null when the policy has none.

latest_patch_checked.description: The date the latest patch was checked, or null when the policy has none.

state.description: The state today (active, security, eol or eol_grace_expired), or null when it cannot be worked out.

note.description: Why the version is answered as end of life without a matched line.

name: run_proctor_check
title: Run PROCTOR on an app

path.description: App folder, inside the project root. Default: the root itself.

checks.description: Only report these checks. Default: all.

description: Runs the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor check` against the bundled CREED policy and returns its findings (php-floor, unbounded-constraints, lock-committed, portability, mysql56, composer-audit, overrides). It changes nothing in the project, but composer-audit contacts the advisory database, so leave that check out when offline. The path must be inside the project. It reports only: PROCTOR in CI decides pass or fail.

tool.description: The tool that produced the report.

proctor_version.description: The PROCTOR version that ran the check.

app.description: The app folder the check ran on, relative to the project root.

checks_run.description: The checks the report covers, in PROCTOR order.

result.description: pass when no check failed, fail when at least one did.

message.description: The finding message, quoted from the project.

path.description: The file the finding points at, or null when there is none.

line.description: The line the finding points at, or null when there is none.

notice.description: A reminder that PROCTOR in CI decides pass or fail.

name: upgrade_path
title: Plan the upgrade path

path.description: App folder, inside the project root. Default: the root itself.

from_php.description: PHP version the app runs today, major.minor, for example 7.4. Only needed when the project names none (no composer.json, or no php constraint in it); BOOSTER then plans from this version.

to_php.description: Target PHP version, major.minor, for example 8.4. Default: the newest supported one.

to_laravel.description: Target Laravel major version, for example 11. Default: the newest supported one.

description: Plans how to upgrade the app's PHP and/or Laravel, one supported hop at a time, by running BOOSTER's read-only `plan` against the bundled CREED policy. It returns the ordered hops (with the Rector sets and manual notes for each), any warnings, and the exact `booster run` command to start. It changes nothing in the project and needs no network. The path must be inside the project. BOOSTER does the work when you run it; this only shows the way. If BOOSTER refuses because the project names no PHP version, call again with from_php set to the version the app runs (run_proctor_check reports it).

tool.description: The tool that produced the plan.

app.description: The app folder the plan is for, relative to the project root.

project.description: What BOOSTER read from the project manifests, or an empty list when it read nothing.

today.description: The date the plan was made, YYYY-MM-DD.

policy.description: The policy the plan was checked against.

target_php.description: The target PHP version, or null when the plan sets none.

target_laravel.description: The target Laravel version, or null when the plan sets none.

steps.description: The ordered upgrade hops, one supported hop at a time.

warnings.description: The warnings BOOSTER raised about the plan.

next_command.description: The exact booster run command to start the plan.

notice.description: A reminder that the plan changes nothing until booster run does the work.
